root_idea.summary: The root denotes putting something beneath or within another thing while keeping it hidden or secret.
root_idea.development: This orientation appears in burial and concealed insertion, then extends to self-concealment, covert approach, spying, and related specialized camel usages involving hidden or localized treatment.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested Form I imperfect is presented under the normalized perfect citation form.

senses.definition: To hide or put something into earth, dust, or beneath another thing; to bury or thrust it in.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence describes burying a female child in dust. The lexical range includes concealed insertion and, in one reported explanation, forcible or forceful thrusting.

senses.definition: To conceal, obscure, or debase the soul.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic soul-object construction, this is interpreted as hiding the soul from notice, diminishing it through evil works or neglected obedience, or placing it among the righteous despite not belonging to them. The supplied evidence gives no secure QAC word location for this cited construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To apply tar to a camel only on the armpits, inner roots of the thighs, or similar parts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized camel-treatment usage, explicitly described as incomplete or localized anointing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel, to become swollen in the parts called the masāʿir.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separately reported interpretation of the specialized expression دَسَّ البَعِيرَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel, to have a slight case of mange.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Explained as a light, concealed condition of the body.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Tar used to anoint specified parts of camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun for the tar applied to the armpits, inner thigh-roots, or comparable parts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become hidden or buried, or to conceal or insert oneself beneath something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reflexive or intransitive counterpart of hidden insertion, including becoming buried or putting oneself beneath another thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To approach someone secretly in order to bring calumnies or hostile reports.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative social usage involving covert approach and the delivery of slander.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The concealment of guile or artifice.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun describing hidden cunning or a concealed scheme.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person secretly sent to obtain and report information; a spy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may denote one whom a group sends covertly to investigate and bring back news.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hypocritical people who enter among Quran reciters despite not being of them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized plural usage for covert or deceptive entrants among a religious group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A secret approach or machination, especially one involving covertly bringing calumnies to someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is also used for a secret scheme or similar concealed maneuver.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who enters frequently; figuratively, a disposition or inherited trait that quietly enters and acts in a person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The figurative usage occurs in the saying that a natural disposition enters and affects the person in whom it is engendered.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel, treated with tar on the specified body parts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial description of a camel subjected to the specialized localized tar treatment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A snake that remains beneath earth or dust.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical derivative associated with something concealed under the ground.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Covers concealed or buried insertion and the Quranic soul-object usage.
Covers localized camel tar treatment and the reported swelling interpretation.
Covers becoming hidden, buried, or inserted beneath something.
Covers concealment of guile or artifice.
Covers the covert informer or spy.
Covers the specialized plural for hypocritical entrants among Quran reciters.
Covers secret approach with calumny and secret machination.
Covers frequent entering and the figurative inherited disposition.
Covers the passive participle applied to a camel treated with tar.

cautions: The Quranic soul-object usage has several reported interpretations, including concealment, debasement, and illicit insertion among the righteous; these are presented as one constructional sense rather than as a single fixed English equivalent.
The historical Quran citation attached to that soul-object discussion is not converted into a modern verse location because the supplied QAC occurrence list does not independently provide one.
